key_insight: A world model can be learned directly from unlabeled, in-the-wild videos by discovering a compact latent action space that disentangles controllable actions from other factors, enabling prediction of action consequences without explicit action labels.
problem_solved: Removes the dependence on costly action labels by learning latent action representations and transition dynamics from raw video, allowing predictive, planning-capable models to be trained on large-scale, real-world visual data.
method: Train a self-supervised world model that encodes video frames into disentangled latents separating controllable (action) factors from environment/context.
Learn a compact latent action space and a transition/prediction module that predicts future observations conditioned on inferred latent actions.
Use temporal consistency and disentanglement/regularization objectives to make the latent actions interpretable and useful for planning.
impact: Enables scalable creation of predictive models and planners from unlabeled video, lowering the barrier for deploying world-model-based agents in real-world and robotics applications where action labels are unavailable or expensive.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw video → encoder (separates action vs context latents) → latent action + transition model → predicted future frames
Latent-space visualization: 2D/3D embedding showing disentangled action trajectories and how interventions move points in latent space
Before/after prediction panel: ground-truth future frames vs model predictions conditioned on inferred latent actions
Schematic comparison: labeled-action training vs latent-action training (data-efficiency and scalability callouts)
paper_title: Learning Latent Action World Models In The Wild
paper_authors: Quentin Garrido, Tushar Nagarajan, Basile Terver, Nicolas Ballas, Yann LeCun
